lede: Epoch 20 is the scored Fashion checkpoint: test BPD 3.263. Inverse samples stay fragments and blobs, while the VAE grids stay readable.
title: Multi-scale RealNVP
question: Does the coupling flow assign high likelihood to grayscale MNIST and invert into recognizable samples?
process: Grayscale pixels in \([0,1]\) are uniformly dequantized and passed through a logit. `CouplingLayer` in `src/mnist_realnvp/model.py` holds the masked coordinates fixed and updates the rest, \( y = m \odot x + (1-m) \odot (x e^{s} + t) \), with \( s = \mathrm{scale}\cdot\tanh(\cdot) \). The log-determinant adds \( s \) only on the changed coordinates. `MultiScaleFlow` squeezes space into channels, couples, and factors half the channels out at \(14\times 14\) and again at \(7\times 7\); the base density on those three latent pieces is a standard normal, and samples invert that map. Optuna ran two 1-epoch trials on digits. The wider one (64 channels, 4 layers, scale 2, learning rate \(10^{-3}\), no weight decay, batch 128) reached validation NLL 860.1 and BPD 1.583. The narrow one (32 channels, scale 1, learning rate \(10^{-4}\), weight decay \(10^{-6}\), batch 64) reached NLL 1050.1, which is BPD 1.932 under the same conversion. Fashion trained 20 epochs from the wider setting, with no search of its own. `evaluation_test_fashion.json` records test BPD 3.263. The digits eval stage never wrote a test file.

opening.summary: Fashion test BPD moves from 3.582 on the first point of `bpd_fashion.png` to 3.263 at epoch 20. That last point is bold: it is the checkpoint the training loop kept, and it matches the test file. A uniform 8-bit image would cost 8 bits per pixel, so 3.263 is a real density. The inverse samples are still soft.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: Epoch 1 is the first test point on bpd_fashion.png, BPD 3.582. The train curve on that figure starts near 4.11. Most of the drop happens in these early epochs. Intermediate epochs were drawn to the PNG and were not written as a series.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion bits per dimension. Epoch 20 is the right-hand end.

marks.summary: Epoch 20 is bold because it is the scored checkpoint. evaluation_test_fashion.json records test NLL 1773.2 and BPD 3.263 on 10,000 images, the same BPD as the last point of bpd_fashion.png. Train on that split is NLL 1763.6 and BPD 3.245. The loop keeps the last weights, and the curve is flat here rather than rising, so this is the best likelihood the run left on disk. It is a partial success: 3.263 beats an 8-bit uniform code, and the inverse samples are still garment blobs. A tight grayscale flow sits nearer 1 bit per dimension. The digits search, after one epoch, was already at validation BPD 1.583.
marks.frameCaption: 64 inverse-flow Fashion samples from the epoch-20 checkpoint.

marks.label: trial 0 picked
marks.summary: Trial 0 is bold because it minimizes validation NLL. best_params.json stores hidden channels 64, 4 coupling layers, scale 2, learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0, batch 128, validation NLL 860.1, validation BPD 1.583. The objective was likelihood after one epoch, two folds, on digits. Generation quality was not in the score. Fashion reused these values.

marks.label: trial 1 narrow
marks.answers: How could the results be improved?
marks.summary: Trial 1 changed every free knob the other way: hidden channels 32, scale 1, learning rate 0.0001, weight decay 1e-6, batch 64. Validation NLL rose to 1050.1 (BPD 1.932). The wider, faster step won. Two trials and one epoch is the whole search that is on disk. The Plotly files optimization_history.html, param_importances.html, parallel_coordinate.html, and parameter_slice.html show this same pair.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: samples.png inverts the digits flow. A few cells suggest a loop or a stem. Most cells are hooks, specks, and broken junctions. The VAE and f-VAE sample grids later in the report still read as digits. This grid does not.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: samples_fashion.png draws the standard normal through the inverse. A few cells suggest a shirt, a trouser leg, a bag, or a boot. Most are smeared gray masses. The Fashion VAE samples keep those garment types readable.

marks.valueText: encode then invert · clothes stay sharp
marks.summary: reconstructions_fashion.png encodes eight Fashion test images and inverts the flow. The boot, the shirt, the trousers, and the plaid stay sharp. The coupling inverse preserves a real image. The soft sample grid is the prior.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion test images above, encode-and-invert below.

marks.label: Digits test file
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: The digits checkpoint, loss.png, bpd.png, and samples.png are on disk. evaluation_test.json is not, because mnist_realnvp_eval did not run. The digits likelihood we can quote exactly is the 1-epoch search, validation BPD 1.583. bpd.png shows the longer train falling and flattening, with the test curve under the train curve.
marks.frameCaption: Digits bits per dimension during training.

reflection.worked: The masked coupling and the two squeeze scales are in `CouplingLayer` and `MultiScaleFlow`. Fashion test BPD falls from 3.582 to 3.263, and epoch 20 matches `evaluation_test_fashion.json`. Encode-and-invert returns sharp clothes, so the inverse runs. The wider Optuna trial beat the narrow one, 860.1 against 1050.1.
reflection.unexpected: Inverse samples stay broken on both sets: stroke fragments on digits, soft gray blobs on Fashion. The VAE sample grids are the readable ones. The digits test JSON is absent.
reflection.why: The search is two trials and one epoch, and Fashion inherited the digits hyperparameters. Dequantization plus the logit lets BPD fall by explaining background and a rough silhouette. 3.263 bits per dimension is better than 8 and far from a tight flow near 1. The sharp reconstructions show the blur sits in the prior.
reflection.improve: Run mnist_realnvp_eval on the digits checkpoint so that run has a held-out NLL. Give Fashion its own search, train longer, and keep the reconstruction grid beside the prior samples. If BPD keeps falling while prior samples stay soft, add capacity in the coupling networks.
